heroHeadline: ISM Manufacturing PMI 54.0% in May — 5th Consecutive Expansion Month, New Orders 56.8%; Caixin China PMI 51.8% Diverges Favorably from NBS 50.0 Borderline; Iran MOU Unsigned Day 3 — Brent ~$96.42 (Recovery); June 16 Warsh FOMC + BOJ 15 Days; Section 122 Cliff 52 Days
heroSubtitle: The global recession risk landscape as of June 1, 2026 — Day 18 of the Warsh Fed era — delivered two significant upside surprises in manufacturing data that challenge the dominant narrative of a ~1% Q2 GDP trajectory, even as the Iran Memorandum of Understanding enters its third day unsigned and oil markets partially reverse their May relief rally. The Institute for Supply Management released the US Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index for May 2026 at 54.0% — up 1.3 percentage points from April's 52.7%, marking the fifth consecutive month of manufacturing expansion and the strongest national reading since May 2022. The New Orders sub-index surged to 56.8%, up 2.7 percentage points — the most forward-looking component, implying continued manufacturing momentum into June. ISM's historical correlation with GDP places a 54.0% reading consistent with 2.2% annualized real GDP growth — significantly above the ~1% Q2 projection. This national confirmation follows the Chicago PMI's surge to 62.7 on May 29 (4-year high, largest monthly jump since 2020) and S&P Global's Flash Manufacturing PMI of 55.3 (May 22, 48-month high), completing a triple confirmation of US manufacturing recovery. Caixin Media and S&P Global released the Caixin China Manufacturing PMI for May at 51.8%, beating the 51.4% consensus and remaining solidly above the 50-point expansion threshold, despite a modest deceleration from April's 52.2%. Critically, Caixin's 51.8% diverges favorably from the NBS official PMI of 50.0% released on May 31 — a divergence that reflects the structural difference between the two surveys: the NBS primarily captures large state-owned enterprises and export-oriented manufacturers (most exposed to Iran war Middle East demand destruction and the US 31.6% effective tariff barrier), while Caixin surveys the SME and private sector (benefiting from domestic demand, new customer acquisition, and technology supply chain investment). Caixin also reported that input and output price increases slowed for the first time in six to seven months — a disinflation signal that matters for both the PBOC's policy calculus and for global supply chain inflation inputs. Despite the manufacturing upside, the Iran MOU situation continues to dominate geopolitical and oil market uncertainty. As of June 1, the tentative 60-day Memorandum of Understanding drafted by US and Iranian negotiators on approximately May 28 remains unsigned — Day 3 of an unsigned framework that markets initially interpreted as a near-certainty. Brent crude recovered to approximately $96.42 per barrel as of 8:30 a.m. ET on June 1, up from the May 30 close of $92.56, as the oil market partially reinstated a risk premium on deal uncertainty (notably, WTI also rose sharply intraday). The partial price recovery signals that market participants no longer view the deal as imminent, and the June 5 window — coinciding with the May Non-Farm Payrolls report — is now the next critical convergence point. The five-step critical path as of June 1: June 5 (May payrolls + Iran MOU signature window) → June 16-17 (Kevin Warsh's inaugural FOMC with first Summary of Economic Projections and dot plot, coinciding with the Bank of Japan's June 16 meeting where a rate hike to 1.00% is priced at 65-77% probability — the most consequential simultaneous global monetary policy event of 2026) → July 24 (Section 122 tariff cliff, 52 days). Warsh's three structural reform pillars — accelerating balance sheet reduction from $6.7T toward $4-5T, eliminating calendar-based forward guidance, and shifting the inflation gauge from PCE to trimmed-mean PCE — maintain structural upward pressure on long-end Treasury yields regardless of the encouraging manufacturing data. Goldman Sachs maintains a 30% US recession probability; JPMorgan 35%; Moody's Analytics 49% — all set before today's ISM beat; updates are expected in the coming days.
